definitions.explanation: A road or street with rows of trees planted along one or both sides. A common feature of parks, boulevards, and scenic routes in Japan.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{並木道|なみきみち}を{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked along a cherry tree-lined road.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{並木道|なみきみち}の{葉|は}が{赤|あか}く{色|いろ}づく。
examples.english: In autumn, the leaves on the tree-lined road turn red.

examples.japanese: この{並木道|なみきみち}は{百年以上|ひゃくねんいじょう}の{歴史|れきし}があり、{市民|しみん}に{愛|あい}されている。
examples.english: This tree-lined avenue has over a hundred years of history and is loved by the citizens.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {並木|なみき} (row of trees) and {道|みち} (road). Used to describe scenic streets, especially those famous for seasonal beauty like cherry blossoms in spring or colorful leaves in autumn. {並木|なみき} alone can also refer to a row of trees along a street.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桜|さくら}の{並木道|なみきみち} (cherry tree-lined road)
- {銀杏|いちょう}の{並木道|なみきみち} (ginkgo tree-lined avenue)
- {並木道|なみきみち}を{歩|ある}く (to walk along a tree-lined road)
- {並木道|なみきみち}を{散歩|さんぽ}する (to stroll along a tree-lined road)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {並木|なみき}: row of trees — the trees themselves, not necessarily the road
- {街路樹|がいろじゅ}: roadside trees — individual trees planted along streets
